purpose: Exploratory development screen: does a fixed piecewise-linear numerical encoding (PLE) raise compressed shared Adam macro-F1?
hypothesis: PLE improved central macro-F1 over a matched-capacity raw network in the archived official39 pilot; the same fixed encoding may lift the federated model at higher payload.
encoding: Per feature, unique quantiles at linspace(0,1,17) of the 500,000 standardized fit rows (all 39 features, no labels); cumulative clipped ramps as in archived flow_representation.encode; constant features one zero column. Fixed preprocessing outside the model.
learning_rates: Historical selections reused (central 0.001, compressed 0.003); no new search
sampling: Historical sample RNG: central per step, compressed per (round, client, step) with 20 clients x 500 rows; sample chains must equal historical central_adam and block128
references: Historical central_adam (alarm-results.json) and block128 (block-compression-results.json) at the same calibration split
evaluation: Central model; compressed delivered replica (as historical block128). Same grouped calibration/audit split and four FAR targets.
screen_scope: Gate applies to compressed_ple only; central_ple is reported to show whether the representation gain transfers to this cohort. Payload is reported, not gated.
limitations: Bins fitted on pooled fit rows (a centralized simplification like the shared scaler). One seed, one partition, previously examined development rows. Exploratory only.
